gen_risks.description: Delays or defects in delivering the internal CRM system MVP by November 2025 could disrupt the expression of interest process for Cohort 1 schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize core MVP functionality for onboarding and maintain manual fallback support procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Onboarding delays during the transition of National School Breakfast Programme (NSBP) schools in July 2026 could lead to gaps in breakfast provision before Cohort 2 starts in September 2026.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all NSBP schools and initiate early communication and onboarding ahead of July 2026.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Schools with higher food procurement costs, external catering contracts, or high staffing ratios may be unable to operate within the standard grant funding model.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy delivery advisers to assist schools in transitioning to low-cost in-house food provision and standard staffing ratios.
gen_risks.evidence: Schools delivering their offer in-house, keeping food costs low, and staffing broadly in line with standard ratios were generally able to operate within the funding available.

gen_risks.description: Lack of timely approval or budget confirmation from HM Treasury for future financial years could delay or truncate national rollout beyond Year 1.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit early evaluation data from Year 1 and robust multi-year business cases to HM Treasury.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

gen_risks.description: Delays in passing the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill through Parliament could delay the implementation of the statutory duty on schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Drive voluntary adoption via Section 14 grant funding while actively supporting legislative progress.
gen_risks.evidence: the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club

gen_risks.description: Physical space constraints in school buildings may prevent primary schools from safely accommodating all pupils attending breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical estate advisers to evaluate school premises and recommend layout adaptations.
gen_risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Shortages of skilled delivery personnel within DfE or supervisory staff within schools could impede effective breakfast club delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure framework advisers and provide dedicated funding to local authorities to boost delivery capacity.
gen_risks.evidence: and the availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Perceived administrative complexity or operational burden could reduce school leadership willingness to join optional early cohorts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a simplified flat-rate funding model and direct self-service support via the CRM system.
gen_risks.evidence: This should ease the burden and potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme.

gen_risks.description: Schools may fail to comply with statutory school food standards due to local catering or supply chain limitations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide standardized menu guidelines and compliant food supplier guidance to participating schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Day-to-day fluctuations in daily pupil attendance could cause volatile funding allocations and budget unpredictability for schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide a fixed £25 daily baseline amount to cover fixed operational costs regardless of attendance variation.
gen_risks.evidence: there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
